title: A buffer with the rule of five
description:
Write an owning byte buffer that copies and moves correctly.

```
a = 16 bytes
b = a (copy): different memory, same bytes
c = std::move(a): a is now empty, c has the bytes
self-assignment safe, no leaks
```
hints: Copy-and-swap: `Buffer& operator=(Buffer other) noexcept { swap(*this, other); return *this; }` handles self-assignment for free (lesson 5.05).
The move constructor steals the pointer with `std::exchange(other.m_data, nullptr)` and sets `other.m_size` to 0.
requirements: Destructor, copy constructor, copy assignment, move constructor and move assignment.
Copy assignment uses copy-and-swap; moves are `noexcept`.
stretch: Replace all five with a `std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]>` member plus a copy constructor, and see which you no longer need.
